g.text: A rate limiter controls how many requests a client can make within a specific timeframe.

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: It acts like a traffic controller for your API - allowing, for example, 100 requests per minute from a user,

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: then rejecting excess requests with an HTTP 429 "Too Many Requests" response. Rate limiters prevent abuse,

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: protect your servers from being overwhelmed by bursts of traffic, and ensure fair usage across all users.

g.text: X-RateLimit-Limit: The rate limit ceiling for that request (e.g., "100")

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: X-RateLimit-Remaining: Number of requests left in the current window (e.g., "0")

text.font-family: Comic Shanns, monospace, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: X-RateLimit-Reset: When the rate limit resets, as a Unix timestamp (e.g., "1640995200")
